title: Finite Sums, Powers and Multiples
html:
Let R be a commutative ring.

  1. (Sums.) Let T be a set with a function +:T×T→T and an element 0∈T with 0+u=u for every u∈T. For a sequence (ui)i∈N in T there is exactly one way to define ∑i=0kui∈T, for k∈N, such that ∑i=00ui=u0,∑i=0k+1ui=∑i=0kui+uk+1, starting from the empty sum 0. The sum ∑i=0kui depends only on u0,…,uk; so a finite list u0,…,uk has a sum, computed from any extension of the list to a sequence. Likewise, a finite list s1,…,sr in R has a product ∏j=1rsj, with ∏j=10sj=1 and ∏j=1r+1sj=(∏j=1rsj)sr+1.

  2. (Rules for sums in R.) For k∈N, c∈R and elements ui,vi∈R:

    (Σ1) ∑i=0k(ui+vi)=∑i=0kui+∑i=0kvi;

    (Σ2) c∑i=0kui=∑i=0kcui;

    (Σ3) for j∈N: if ui=0 for every i≤k with i≠j, then ∑i=0kui=uj when j≤k, and ∑i=0kui=0 when j>k;

    (Σ4) −∑i=0kui=∑i=0k(−ui).

  3. (Powers.) For s∈R and n∈N, s0:=1 and sn+1:=sns define sn for every n, and for all s,t∈R and m,n∈N, sm+n=smsn,(sm)n=smn,(st)n=sntn.

  4. (Multiples.) For all a,b∈R and m,n∈Z, (m+n)⋅a=m⋅a+n⋅a,m⋅(a+b)=m⋅a+m⋅b,(m⋅a)b=m⋅(ab),(m⋅1)a=m⋅a,(mn)⋅a=m⋅(n⋅a).
